_comment: Authored summary targets — plan.md §9. Keyed by dataset record id. Merge with: npm --prefix api run merge:dataset
_batch: 007 — GREY and GREEN weighting to correct the band skew. Several patients state an expectation or a fear that the tick-boxes never asked about; where that would change how the consult opens, it goes in what-to-ask rather than being dropped as non-clinical.
grey_hip-004:
**Snapshot** — 68y man, Ranchi. Lower back pain for more than a year, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain is groin-dominant rather than back-dominant
- Hip stiffness putting on socks and getting out of a car
- Radiation stops at the buttock, left side
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Groin-dominant pain with hip stiffness on dressing, and no radiation past the buttock, points away from the spine and towards the hip joint.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Internal rotation range, and whether it reproduces the groin pain
- Whether pain is worst on weight-bearing or first steps after rest
- He wrote *(translated)*: "Doctor, I do not want an operation. Please suggest some other treatment." Worth saying early that a hip assessment is not a surgical decision.
grey_shoulder-004:
**Snapshot** — 45y woman, desk job. Neck pain with arm pain, 3 to 12 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Arm pain worse on reaching overhead
- Pain stays above the elbow, at the right shoulder only
- No hand numbness, no grip loss, no dexterity change
- Working with difficulty; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Overhead-provoked arm pain that stops above the elbow, with no hand symptoms, points to the shoulder joint rather than a cervical root.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Painful arc, and whether passive movement hurts as much as active
- Impingement tests and rotator cuff power
- She wrote *(translated)*: "I do not want an operation. Please suggest some other treatment." Most shoulder impingement is managed without surgery — worth saying so.
grey_vascular-002:
**Snapshot** — 70y woman, shop or business. Leg pain and difficulty walking, 3 to 12 months.

**Key findings**
- Walking limited to 100–500 metres, both legs
- Pain settles on standing still alone — no need to sit or bend
- Diabetes and tobacco use
- Radiation stops at the buttock; no numbness or weakness
- No red flags

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Relief on standing still, without flexion, is the discriminator separating this from spinal claudication. With diabetes and smoking alongside, a vascular cause is the stronger query.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Peripheral pulses and ankle-brachial index
- Any rest pain, night pain in the foot, or slow-healing ulcers
- Foot inspection, given the diabetes
- She wrote *(translated)*: "Travelling is very difficult, sitting in a bus or auto is hard."
grey_inflammatory-002:
**Snapshot** — 31y woman, student. Lower back pain for 3 to 12 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes
- Pain improves with movement and worsens with rest
- Sleep disturbed sometimes
- No radiation, numbness, weakness or red flags
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Prolonged morning stiffness with exercise-responsive pain, at 31 with months of symptoms, fits an inflammatory rather than mechanical pattern.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Alternating buttock pain, or heel and chest wall pain
- Personal or family history of psoriasis, uveitis or inflammatory bowel disease
- Whether anti-inflammatories help dramatically, which would support the pattern
- Whether pain wakes her in the second half of the night
grey_widespread-002:
**Snapshot** — 29y man, driver. Lower back pain for more than a year, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain in many parts of the body with constant tiredness
- Sleep disturbed most nights
- The back pain itself has no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; managing daily tasks independently
- Painkillers only, partial relief

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Widespread pain with persistent fatigue and no localising spinal findings suggests the back pain is one part of a broader picture.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Which other sites hurt, and whether they preceded the back pain
- Sleep quality separately from pain — unrefreshing sleep is part of the pattern
- Driving hours, and whether the fatigue is affecting his safety at work
- He wrote *(translated)*: "Everyone in my family has this problem. My father also had back pain."
grey_unclear-002:
**Snapshot** — 35y man, driver. Selected "none of these" as the main complaint, so the questionnaire never showed the spine branches.

**Key findings**
- No spinal complaint selected
- All ten red-flag questions answered no
- The back, neck, function and treatment sections were never reached
- His note mentions medication giving partial relief, though no treatment question was shown
- There is no symptom detail on file to review

**Supporting the triage verdict** — The complaint does not match any spine pattern the questionnaire can route on. This is a gap in the intake rather than a clinical finding.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- What the problem actually is, in his own words
- He wrote *(translated)*: "The medicine gives some relief but the pain does not go completely." So there is a pain problem the form did not capture.
- What he is taking, and who prescribed it
grey_hip-005:
**Snapshot** — 64y man, farm and labour work. Lower back pain for more than a year, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain is groin-dominant rather than back-dominant
- Hip stiffness putting on socks and getting out of a car
- Radiation stops at the buttock, left side
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Daily painkillers to keep working

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Groin-dominant pain with hip stiffness on dressing, and no radiation past the buttock, points away from the spine and towards the hip joint.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Internal rotation range, and whether it reproduces the groin pain
- Whether squatting or sitting cross-legged has become difficult
- He wrote *(translated)*: "I have to take medicine daily or I cannot work. Is there a permanent cure?" He is asking about cure, not management.

green_acute_mechanical-003:
**Snapshot** — 31y man, desk job. Lower back pain for 2 to 6 weeks after lifting, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Sudden onset after lifting or bending
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation past the thigh
- No numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Rest only; no medication or other treatment tried

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Under six weeks, mechanical onset, no neurological findings and no red flags. This sits inside the natural-history window.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- He wrote *(translated)*: "I have not had any treatment elsewhere, I came straight to you." First contact, so expectations are unset and easy to shape.
- Whether rest means complete rest, which tends to slow recovery
- Which symptoms should bring him back sooner
green_untreated_chronic-002:
**Snapshot** — 56y woman, shop or business. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Working, with difficulty
- Painkillers only — no physiotherapy, injections or surgery
- No red flags on any of the ten screening questions

**Supporting the triage verdict** — More than six weeks of pain with no neurological findings, and structured conservative care not yet attempted.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- She writes that her mother had the same problem and needed an operation, and she is worried this is the same — that fear is likely why she came
- Standing hours at the shop, and whether the work can be modified
- Whether supervised physiotherapy is accessible to her
advisory_pregnancy-003:
**Snapshot** — 24y woman, shop or business, pregnant. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pregnancy reported — imaging and medication options are restricted
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Taking painkillers, unspecified
- No physiotherapy yet

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Six weeks or more of uncomplicated back pain, no neurological findings, and conservative care not yet attempted.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Gestation, and whether she is under obstetric care
- Exactly which painkillers, and on whose advice — this needs checking first
- Whether pelvic girdle pain describes this better than lumbar pain
- Standing hours at the shop, and what adjustments are available
advisory_recent_imaging-002:
**Snapshot** — 32y man, shop or business. Lower back pain for 3 to 12 months, 5/10, no radiation.

**Key findings**
- MRI within the last 3 months; films and report not yet seen
- Pain stays in the back — no numbness, weakness or red flags
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Painkillers only; no physiotherapy yet
- Reports the pain is affecting his mood

**Supporting the triage verdict** — Months of pain with no neurological findings and no structured conservative care attempted. The existing scan does not change that.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- Ask him to bring the films and full report, not just the conclusion
- He wrote *(translated)*: "The pain has made me irritable, my mood is not good." Worth asking about directly.
- What he was told about the scan, and what he now expects
advisory_free_text-002:
**Snapshot** — 58y man, farm and labour work. Lower back pain for 6 weeks to 3 months, 5/10.

**Key findings**
- Pain stays in the back — no radiation, numbness or weakness
- Walking unrestricted; sleep undisturbed
- Working, with difficulty
- Painkillers only — no physiotherapy, injections or surgery
- No red flags on any of the ten screening questions

**Supporting the triage verdict** — More than six weeks of pain with no neurological findings, and structured conservative care not yet attempted.

**What the doctor may want to ask**
- He wrote *(translated)*: "It would be better if the whole check-up could be done in one visit, coming again and again is difficult." Manual work and travel cost may limit follow-up — front-load what you can.
- Lifting demands at work, and whether they can be reduced
- Whether physiotherapy is reachable from where he lives
green_acute_mechanical-004:
